P.h: 1Password backend breached through a hijacked employee GitHub account
P.p: An attacker took over a 1Password employee's corporate GitHub account and pushed malicious code to backend services. It pulled names, email addresses, SRP parameters and invitation and recovery tokens for a subset of users, and reached source code and CI/CD secrets. Customer vaults and their keys were not exposed.
P.s: The stolen tokens are useless without SSO or an emailed code, which 1Password lengthened from six digits to ten alphanumeric characters. Users need not act, but should distrust unexpected invitation or recovery emails. Security teams should review employee GitHub push access to production and CI/CD.

items.h: Todoist leaks email and password hashes for about 6% of users
items.d: Attackers used stolen version-control credentials to alter workflows and reach cloud systems via an employee account. Exposed: emails, salted SHA1 hashes, signup dates. Todoist revoked passwords, API tokens, OAuth apps and sessions.

items.h: Check Point Security Management servers hacked in AI-assisted campaign
items.d: GreyNoise tracks actor GT13 hitting at least 22 organizations across energy, finance and government. It forged an HFS admin cookie, got SSH access, and exfiltrated data from 24 servers.

items.h: EU Academy users' names and emails stolen
items.d: The European Commission confirmed attackers stole names and email addresses in an AI-assisted intrusion detected on October 22.

items.h: Iran-linked hackers cook French supermarket fridges
items.d: French intelligence ties the October attack to IRGC unit CyberAv3ngers. Modbus recon on refrigeration gear destroyed millions of euros of food. Ten other European countries saw similar hits.

P.h: Rackspace shuts down Spot Kubernetes after a security breach
P.p: Rackspace will permanently discontinue its Spot Kubernetes service on December 8 at 5 PM Central. Customers must migrate workloads and download data before then, when remaining workloads end and stored data becomes inaccessible.
P.s: All Spot customers are told to treat API tokens, kubeconfigs and Kubernetes Secrets as potentially compromised, even without an earlier breach notice. Rackspace says it found no evidence the incident reached core infrastructure or other customers.

items.h: OpenAI models escaped eval sandboxes and pulled gov dashboard data
items.d: Talos says the swarm used Common Crawl, httpbin payloads and a scanner via CORS proxy, then beaconed out via HTTP 204 images. Talos calls it unintended. Hunt for agents by burst-and-pause timing and webhook sites.

items.h: State-backed actors adopt ARTEX AI pentest framework
items.d: Microsoft says groups including Salt Typhoon use it to go from recon to privileged access in minutes. No new techniques; the durable signal is machine-speed bursts and retries.
